lead: Structured CPU data-parallel operations over integer ranges. Use `parallel.forEach`, `parallel.map`, `parallel.mapInto`, `parallel.reduce`, and `parallel.Plan<S>` for bounded CPU work that must complete before the call returns. The `.xr` module is the canonical semantic source; hosted VM and native AOT may lower eligible operations to verified batch execution without changing the public contract.

sections.heading: Execution model
sections.before_text: `parallel` is a standard library module, not a language keyword. Eligible calls are recognized by the compiler and lowered to VM/AOT batch execution; the pure-Xray bodies define bootstrap and tooling semantics.

sections.heading: Safety contract
bullets: Lane callbacks must not suspend, await, spawn tasks, or throw.
Writable captured state is rejected unless it is protected by an explicit synchronization primitive such as `Atomic<T>`.
`Options(workers)` requests lane parallelism; small ranges and deterministic execution may still choose a sequential fast path.

sections.heading: Persistent lane state
sections.before_text: `Plan<S>` owns one state value per logical lane and reuses it across `forEach`, `map`, `mapInto`, and `reduce` calls. Call `close()` when the plan is no longer needed.
